PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL

Mr. Robert Grimes
General Manager
{{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}

Dear Robert,

Thank you for the time you and the shareholders have given us over the past several weeks, and for the candor with which you described both what the business needs from its balance sheet and what its owners need from the business. This letter sets out the terms on which Quillon Harbor Advisors LLC will act as financial advisor to {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} on the recapitalization we discussed, and we have tried to write it so that nothing in it promises more than a financing process can deliver.

Our work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}} and has a single object: to put in front of the shareholders a financing, or a clear choice between financings, that refinances the company's existing bank facility and provides the liquidity the owners have asked for, on terms the company's cash flow can carry through its slower months. To get there we will review the business plan and the monthly accounts, build a financial model that reconciles to the company's own records, and give the shareholders a written comparison of the capital structures open to them, with our recommendation. We are not engaged to raise equity or to find a buyer for the company, and if the shareholders' thinking moves in either direction we will talk with you about whether that work needs a letter of its own.

Once the shareholders have chosen a structure, we will prepare a financing memorandum, together with a short summary for first contact that describes the company by sector and revenue band only, and we will propose a list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}} for your approval before any of them is approached. We will then manage the outreach, the confidentiality agreements and the management meetings, compare the proposals that come back, recommend the lender or lenders we believe the company should proceed with, and support you and your counsel through the negotiation of the credit documents to closing.

I will lead the engagement myself and will attend every meeting with the shareholders. Robert Turner, an Associate, will manage it day to day, building the model and the memorandum and keeping the data room and the weekly agenda in order, while Sarah Fletcher, an Advisory Associate, will run the approach to financing sources and keep the contact log that records it. You will be our single point of contact at the company, which keeps the circle of people who know about the process as small as you would like it to be.

The schedule below sets out what we will deliver, in the order we expect to deliver it. The timing is indicative and counted in weeks from the start of the engagement; the later stages depend on how quickly financing sources respond, and we will tell you promptly, and in writing, if the timetable moves.

rows: Review of the business plan and monthly accounts; financial model reconciled to the company's records
Written comparison of the capital structures open to the company, with our recommendation to the shareholders
Financing memorandum; a short summary for first contact that does not name the company; data room index
Proposed list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}}, for the shareholders' approval before any approach is made
Approach to the approved sources under confidentiality agreements; management meetings; weekly contact log
Side-by-side comparison of the proposals received, and our recommendation on the lender or lenders to proceed with
Support to the company and its counsel through negotiation of the credit documents and closing

blocks.text: Our fee for the engagement is {{fact:f:E-2016-001.fee}}, which we will invoice in installments: the first on signature of this letter, the second when the financing memorandum is released to financing sources, and the balance at closing of the financing. We will also bill reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, chiefly travel to lender meetings, at cost and monthly, we will ask you before incurring any expense that is out of the ordinary, and our invoices are payable within thirty days.

This letter takes effect when you sign it and runs until the financing closes, unless either of us ends it sooner by written notice, which either of us may do at any time. If the engagement ends before closing, the installments already invoiced are the whole of our fee, unless the company closes a financing within twelve months with a source we introduced, in which case the balance falls due at that closing; the paragraphs on confidentiality and on liability survive in any event.

We will hold everything you give us in confidence and use it only for this engagement. Nothing that circulates outside the company before a financing source has signed a confidentiality agreement will name the company, which will be described by sector and revenue band alone, and the name, the memorandum and the data room will follow only once that agreement is in place.

We will rely on the information the company provides without verifying it independently, and we will not give legal, tax or accounting advice, for which the company should look to its own counsel and accountants. Our liability to the company in connection with this engagement is limited to the fees we have received under this letter, except where a loss results from our gross negligence or willful misconduct, and the company agrees to indemnify us against claims by third parties arising from the engagement, other than claims arising from that same negligence or misconduct.

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which our principal office is located, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and any dispute between us that we cannot resolve by discussion will be heard in the courts of that state.

If this letter reflects our understanding, please sign both copies and return one to me. As soon as we have it, Robert Turner will send you our initial information request, and we will hold the first working session with you in the week the engagement begins.
Accepted and agreed on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}:
